trajectory_messages.content:
Implement a feature in the vllm Rust server to attach a request tracking identifier to HTTP responses, similar to the existing functionality in the Python server. Ensure this feature is opt-in and configurable via command-line and JSON configuration.

*   Update the `FrontendConfig` struct in `rust/src/server/src/config.rs`:
    *   Add a `pub enable_request_id_headers: bool` field.
    *   Default this field to `false`.

*   Modify the `SharedRuntimeArgs` struct in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli.rs`:
    *   Add a `pub enable_request_id_headers: bool` field.
    *   Annotate with `#[arg(long)]` for the `--enable-request-id-headers` CLI flag.
    *   Annotate with `#[serde(default)]` for JSON deserialization.
    *   Ensure `to_frontend_config()` sets `enable_request_id_headers` to `true` when `--enable-request-id-headers` is used.

*   Adjust the `AppState` struct in `rust/src/server/src/state.rs`:
    *   Add a `pub enable_request_id_headers: bool` field.
    *   Default this field to `false` in `AppState::new()`.
    *   Implement a `with_request_id_headers(self, enabled: bool) -> Self` method to set this field.

*   Implement HTTP response behavior based on `enable_request_id_headers`:
    *   If `enable_request_id_headers` is `false`, do not include an `x-request-id` header.
    *   If `enable_request_id_headers` is `true`:
        *   If the incoming request lacks an `X-Request-Id` header, generate a 32 ASCII hex digit UUID v4 and include it as `x-request-id`.
        *   If the incoming request includes an `X-Request-Id` header, echo this value in the `x-request-id` response header.

*   Ensure the `serve` subcommand:
    *   Recognizes the `--enable-request-id-headers` flag.
    *   Produces a `FrontendConfig` with `enable_request_id_headers = true` when the flag is used.

*   Ensure the `frontend` subcommand:
    *   Recognizes the `--args-json` with `"enable_request_id_headers":true`.
    *   Produces a `FrontendConfig` with `enable_request_id_headers = true` when specified.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the relevant files to understand the codebase structure.

9	/// How the HTTP server obtains its listening socket.
10	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
11	pub enum HttpListenerMode {
12	    /// Bind a fresh TCP listener on the given host/port.
13	    BindTcp { host: String, port: u16 },
14	    /// Bind a fresh Unix domain listener on the given filesystem path.
15	    BindUnix { path: String },
16	    /// Adopt an already-open listening socket inherited from a supervisor
17	    /// process.
18	    InheritedFd { fd: i32 },
19	}

21	/// Which coordinator implementation should be active when one is present for a
22	/// frontend client.
23	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
24	pub enum CoordinatorMode {
25	    /// Do not run a coordinator at all.
26	    None,
27	    /// Run the Rust in-process coordinator for managed `serve` deployments, if
28	    /// there are multiple engines and the model is MoE.
29	    MaybeInProc,
30	    /// Connect to an external coordinator owned by another process.
31	    External { address: String },
32	}

34	/// Normalized runtime configuration for the minimal OpenAI-compatible server.
35	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
36	pub struct Config {
37	    /// Frontend-to-engine transport setup.
38	    pub transport_mode: TransportMode,
39	    /// Requested frontend-side coordinator behavior.
40	    pub coordinator_mode: CoordinatorMode,
41	    /// Backend model identifier used for engine-core loading.
42	    pub model: String,
43	    /// Model name(s) exposed to clients via the OpenAI API. When non-empty,
44	    /// the first entry is used as the primary ID in responses and all entries
45	    /// are accepted in requests. When empty, falls back to `model`.
46	    pub served_model_name: Vec<String>,
47	    /// HTTP listener setup.
48	    pub listener_mode: HttpListenerMode,
49	    /// Tool-call parser selection.
50	    pub tool_call_parser: ParserSelection,
51	    /// Reasoning parser selection.
52	    pub reasoning_parser: ParserSelection,
53	    /// Chat renderer selection.
54	    pub renderer: RendererSelection,
55	    /// Server-default chat template override, as a file path or inline
56	    /// template.
57	    pub chat_template: Option<String>,
58	    /// Server-default keyword arguments merged into every chat-template render.
59	    pub default_chat_template_kwargs: Option<HashMap<String, Value>>,
60	    /// How to serialize `message.content` for chat-template rendering.
61	    pub chat_template_content_format: ChatTemplateContentFormatOption,
62	    /// Log a summary line for each completed request.
63	    pub enable_log_requests: bool,
64	    /// When `true`, suppress periodic stats logging (throughput, queue depth,
65	    /// cache usage).
66	    pub disable_log_stats: bool,
67	    /// TCP port for the gRPC Generate service. When `None`, no gRPC server is
68	    /// started.
69	    pub grpc_port: Option<u16>,
70	    /// Maximum time to wait for active HTTP/gRPC requests to drain on shutdown.
71	    pub shutdown_timeout: Duration,
72	}
73	
74	impl Config {
75	    /// Validate frontend configuration that can be checked before engine
76	    /// startup.
77	    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
78	        vllm_chat::validate_parser_overrides(&self.tool_call_parser, &self.reasoning_parser)?;
79	
80	        Ok(())
81	    }
82	
83	    /// Return the number of engines implied by the configured transport mode.
84	    pub fn engine_count(&self) -> usize {
85	        match &self.transport_mode {
86	            TransportMode::HandshakeOwner { engine_count, .. }
87	            | TransportMode::Bootstrapped { engine_count, .. } => *engine_count,
88	        }
89	    }
90	
91	    /// Resolve the effective coordinator mode.
92	    pub fn effective_coordinator_mode(
93	        &self,
94	        model_is_moe: bool,
95	    ) -> Option<EngineCoreCoordinatorMode> {
96	        match &self.coordinator_mode {
97	            CoordinatorMode::None => None,
98	            CoordinatorMode::MaybeInProc => {
99	                if model_is_moe && self.engine_count() > 1 {
100	                    Some(EngineCoreCoordinatorMode::InProc)
101	                } else {
102	                    None
103	                }
104	            }
105	            CoordinatorMode::External { address } => Some(EngineCoreCoordinatorMode::External {
106	                address: address.clone(),
107	            }),
108	        }
109	    }
110	}

47	    pub fn try_parse_from<I, T>(itr: I) -> Result<Self, clap::Error>
48	    where
49	        I: IntoIterator<Item = T>,
50	        T: Into<OsString>,
51	    {
52	        let args: Vec<OsString> = itr.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect();
53	        let repartitioned_args = repartition_managed_engine_args::<Self>(&args, Some("serve"))?;
54	        <Self as Parser>::try_parse_from(&repartitioned_args).inspect(|cli| {
55	            if let Command::Serve(serve) = &cli.command
56	                && serve.debug_cli
57	            {
58	                println!(
59	                    "Original CLI args: {}\n",
60	                    args.join(OsStr::new(" ")).display()
61	                );
62	                println!(
63	                    "Repartitioned CLI args: {}\n",
64	                    repartitioned_args.join(OsStr::new(" ")).display()
65	                );
66	                println!(
67	                    "Passthrough Python args: {}",
68	                    serve.managed_engine.python_args.join(" ")
69	                );
70	                std::process::exit(0);
71	            }
72	        })
73	    }
74	}

## Summary

I implemented the opt-in `x-request-id` response header feature in the vLLM Rust server, mirroring the Python `XRequestIdMiddleware`.

**`rust/src/server/src/config.rs`** — Added `pub enable_request_id_headers: bool` to `Config` (the frontend config struct, re-exported as `Config`).

**`rust/src/cmd/src/cli.rs`** — Added `pub enable_request_id_headers: bool` to `SharedRuntimeArgs` with `#[arg(long)]` (`--enable-request-id-headers`) and `#[serde(default)]`. Wired it through both `into_bootstrapped_config` (frontend path) and `into_managed_config` (serve path) so the flag flows into `Config`.

**`rust/src/server/src/state.rs`** — Added `pub enable_request_id_headers: bool` to `AppState`, defaulted to `false` in `new()`, and added `with_request_id_headers(self, enabled: bool) -> Self`.

**`rust/src/server/src/middleware/request_id.rs`** (new) — `attach_request_id` middleware: passes through untouched when disabled; when enabled, echoes an inbound `X-Request-Id` header or generates a fresh UUID v4 (`Uuid::new_v4().simple()` → 32 lowercase hex digits) and sets it as the `x-request-id` response header.

**`rust/src/server/src/middleware/mod.rs`** — Registered and exported the new middleware.

**`rust/src/server/src/routes.rs`** — Added the middleware layer via `from_fn_with_state`.

**`rust/src/server/src/lib.rs`** — `build_state` now calls `.with_request_id_headers(config.enable_request_id_headers)`.

**`rust/src/server/examples/external_engine_openai_qwen.rs`** — Set the new `Config` field to `false` to keep the example compiling.

Both the `serve` subcommand (via the `--enable-request-id-headers` CLI flag) and the `frontend` subcommand (via `--args-json` with `"enable_request_id_headers":true`) now produce a `Config` with the field set to `true`. No files under `tests/` were touched.
